title: Antioch on the Orontes
lead: Antioch on the Orontes (now Antakya in Turkey) was the capital of the Roman province of Syria and, with Rome and Alexandria, one of the three greatest cities of the empire. It had a large Jewish community. In Acts it is where the disciples were first called Christians (Acts 11:26) and where Barnabas and Saul were sent out on the first mission (Acts 13:1-3); in Galatians it is the scene of Paul's public clash with Cephas (Galatians 2:11-14). Pisidian Antioch, in Galatia, is a different city.

sections.b: Hellenist believers scattered after the death of Stephen brought the good news to Gentiles there (Acts 11:19-21). Barnabas fetched Saul from Tarsus to teach in the church (Acts 11:25-26). The church sent relief to Judea in a famine (Acts 11:27-30) and sent out Barnabas and Saul (Acts 13:1-3). The dispute that led to the Jerusalem meeting began there (Acts 15:1-2), and Galatians 2:11-14 reports a later clash over eating with Gentiles.
